🇺🇸 🤔 Vance cancels summit appearance as US outages fuel blackout rumors Vice President JD Vance was due to sit for an interview at The New York Times’ DealBook Summit on Wednesday. Organizers learned roughly 30 minutes beforehand that he had been asked to stay in Washington for meetings on the outages, summit host Andrew Ross Sorkin said. A global Microsoft outage was followed by a nationwide FAA ground stop, disruptions to JPMorgan and Zelle, and a failure of the National Security Agency’s classified communications network. The disruptions fed online rumors of a 90-day blackout that was supposedly set to begin Nov. 17, the day of a scheduled federal emergency alert test. 👉 Vance told Fox News on Monday that Americans did not need to stockpile food or water. On Wednesday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said officials had found no evidence that the outages were linked or that a coordinated cyberattack was behind them. 👍 Substack | Chat | @geopolitics_prime

NEWS: In a new letter, White House Counsel Will Scharf told congressional Democrats on Wednesday that the Trump administration is under no obligation to comply with their demands for documents and information, arguing that requests from ranking minority members lack the legal authority of formal congressional oversight. Scharf also said requests made during the current Congress would not carry over when Democrats assume committee chairmanships in January. He said the administration would work with incoming committee chairs but warned that any future requests would face scrutiny over their legal authority and legislative purpose. The letter comes as Representative Robert Garcia, the Democrat expected to chair the House Oversight Committee in January, sent letters Wednesday morning to 12 Trump family members, allies and current and former administration officials, directing them to preserve documents ahead of planned investigations into alleged Trump family corruption, the administration’s immigration crackdown and its handling of the Jeffrey Epstein files. Recipients included Vice President JD Vance, White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, Attorney General Todd Blanche and former Chief of Staff Susie Wiles. - Nandita Bose tweet
